claims.text: Increasing Al concentration relative to Mn increases Al diffusion to the alloy surface during high-temperature exposure.
Increasing Si concentration relative to Mn increases transport of passivating elements to the surface.
Surface enrichment in Al leads to formation of α-Al2O3.
Increasing Si alone can promote formation of an α-Al2O3 scale.
Higher Al and/or Si content produces a rapid, uniform, continuous, dense, and coherent α-Al2O3 scale above 900 °C.
A continuous, adherent α-Al2O3 layer acts as a barrier to further oxidation.
The α-Al2O3 barrier inhibits oxide cracking and spallation.
Atmospheric oxidation of CoCrFeNiMn alloys can produce a layered film with a Cr-rich inner oxide and a Mn-rich outer oxide because of outward cation diffusion.
At 900 °C, FeCrMnNiCo forms layered Cr2O3 and Mn2O3 during oxidation.
At 1000–1100 °C, the Mn-rich outer oxide can transform into Mn3O4 and a (Mn,Cr)3O4 oxide.
Mn mobility and low-energy oxide formation can deplete Mn from the alloy, produce pores, and accelerate oxide growth.
Mn-dominated oxidation products are more prone to cracking and spallation than Al/Si-promoted scales.
Alloys with increased Al and/or Si will have lower oxidation weight gain than the Mn-rich baseline.
Alloys with increased Al and/or Si will develop thinner, more coherent, and better-adhered oxide scales than the Mn-rich baseline.
Mn-rich or Al/Si-deficient alloys will form thicker, heterogeneous oxide layers that are unstable and prone to cracking and spallation.
The proposed behavior applies during continuous oxidation above 900 °C.
The proposed behavior also applies in unspecified corrosive atmospheres and to both single- and multiphase metallic solid-solution states.

A result in which the Al/Si-enriched alloy has no coherent continuous α-Al2O3 scale and has oxidation, heterogeneity, and spallation equal to or worse than the Mn-rich baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The intervention permits increasing Si without increasing Al ('Al and/or Si'), while the required mediator is specifically α-Al2O3. A CrFeCoNiSi composition supplies no stated Al source for that mediator.
